title: Fastest Guided Route to a Workstation (A* Pathfinding)
real_world_story: A robot must deliver a part to one specific workstation on a large floor. Exploring the whole floor is wasteful, and the controller already knows roughly where the workstation stands, so it should prefer moves that head toward the target.

real_world_connection.input_represents: Floor plan where 0 is a free aisle and 1 is a blocked machine or storage region
real_world_connection.query_represents: The robot dock cell and the target workstation cell
real_world_connection.algorithm_represents: Expanding the most promising cell first, guided by the remaining straight-line distance to the target

problem_statement: Given an R x C floor plan of 0 (free aisle) and 1 (blocked region), a robot dock cell (sr, sc) and a target workstation cell (dr, dc), find the minimum number of 4-directional moves needed to travel from the dock to the workstation. Blocked cells and moves outside the grid are not allowed.
task: Return the minimum number of moves from the dock to the target workstation, or -1 if the target cannot be reached.
input_format: The first line contains two integers R and C. The next R lines each contain C integers (0 or 1) describing the floor plan. The final line contains four integers sr sc dr dc.
output_format: Print the minimum number of moves from the dock to the workstation, or -1 if unreachable. Print 0 when the dock and the workstation are the same cell.

examples.explanation: The route (0,0) -> (0,1) -> (0,2) -> (1,2) -> (2,2) needs 4 moves, and the Manhattan distance from the dock to the target is also 4, so the heuristic guides the search straight to the goal.

expected_algorithm.name: A* Pathfinding
expected_algorithm.reason: The Manhattan distance to the target is an admissible heuristic on a 4-directional grid, so ordering the frontier by distance travelled plus heuristic estimate returns the optimal route while exploring far fewer cells than an unguided search.

hint: Estimate the remaining work as the number of straight moves still needed to reach the target.
Process the most promising cell first, not simply the oldest cell.
Keep the best known travel cost for every cell so a worse route is never re-explored.
real_world_takeaway: Guided search lets a robot reach a known workstation quickly on a large floor instead of scanning every aisle.
